purpose: Hand-written SSE replays shared by every client. Two things must hold for each entry: a native tool call reaches the caller as a structured proposal, and prose that merely looks like a tool call stays text. There is deliberately no parser for tool calls written in prose - a model that describes a call in a fenced code block or an XML-ish tag has not made one, and promoting it would run a tool the user never approved. `expected` is the single comparison matrix all clients check against.

conventions.line_format: Lines are split on LF; each data block is followed by a blank line; `data: ` includes the space; anthropic/openai_responses each have their own `event:` line before every data line, with the type carried in the body.
conventions.arguments: For the four native cases, the expected arguments is the fully concatenated raw text (a string); gemini's args are a structured object on the wire, and the expected value is compared after JSON normalization (key order is not significant).
conventions.text: expected.text is the raw concatenated body text (not trimmed).

fixtures.scenario: Two function tool calls. Call 0's arguments arrive token by token; call 1 carries an index only on its first fragment and omits it afterwards. finish_reason is tool_calls.
A message item emits text, then a function_call item follows. Its arguments arrive as three function_call_arguments.delta fragments, and the done event repeats the complete value.

A text block followed by a tool_use block. The input arrives as five input_json_delta fragments, the first of them an empty string. message_delta reports stop_reason tool_use, and a ping is interleaved.
A text part in the first chunk and a functionCall part in the last, with structured (unfragmented) arguments and finishReason STOP.
